title: Command Dispatch
objective: Understand how GSD routes commands to the correct handler function

content.value: Once gsd-tools.cjs has the command name from process.argv, it needs to route it to the right handler. GSD uses a straightforward switch statement for this — no dynamic routing, no plugin system, just explicit cases.

Each case maps a command string to a function call. The naming convention is consistent: command functions start with 'cmd' followed by the operation name in camelCase. For example:

  find-phase  -> phase.cmdFindPhase()
  resolve-model -> config.cmdResolveModel()
  commit -> commands.cmdCommit()

Some commands have sub-commands. The 'state' command, for instance, dispatches further based on args[1]:

  state load -> state.cmdStateLoad()
  state advance-plan -> state.cmdAdvancePlan()
  state add-decision -> state.cmdAddDecision()
This two-level dispatch (command -> sub-command) keeps the routing flat and readable. Every command path is visible by scanning the switch statement — no indirection, no dynamic lookups.

successCriteria: You can trace how a command string like 'find-phase' maps to phase.cmdFindPhase() through the switch dispatch
